decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display, it is very close to our existing knowledge base, so our in-house development and production teams can keep improving it and justify retaining it.
The pegboard-back cardboard display remains within our core display competence, and our absorptive capacity is high enough to learn from customer use and refine the format rather than exit it.
This standard cardboard quarter-pallet format overlaps strongly with what we already know and make, so it is more likely to stay as a core offer even in a flat market.
The eighth-pallet display extends our established cardboard POS range in a highly related way, making it relatively easy for us to support and improve commercially.
The wooden display pallet is less closely related to our paper-based core capabilities, so despite some adjacency it offers weaker learning and improvement potential than our cardboard lines.

Although technically close to our core, the media-focused quarter-pallet display is a narrower application, and in a flat market we would reallocate resources toward more broadly reusable display formats.
